item.title: Pfizer–BioNTech Halt U.S. COVID-19 Trial Amid Enrollment Collapse—Signal of Scientific Friction or Market Reality?
item.description: Pfizer and BioNTech have halted a large U.S. clinical trial of their updated COVID-19 vaccine in healthy adults aged 50–64, citing an inability to recruit sufficient participants. The trial, designed to meet stricter requirements from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration,sought up to 30,000 participants but collapsed under low demand, stringent eligibility criteria, and declining public interest in boosters. item.title: Canada Relaunches Vaccine Injury Program Amid Backlog, Transparency Concerns
item.description: The Canadian government, led by Health Minister Marjorie Michel, has relaunched its national vaccine injury compensation system under a new framework—the Vaccine Impact Assistance Program (VIAP)—now administered directly by the Public Health Agency of Canada. Announced March 31, 2026, the program replaces a third-party model and aims to improve efficiency, transparency, and claimant support following mounting criticism over delays and backlog management. A Structural Reset—But Why Now?

item.title: AN OPEN LETTER TO DR. JAY BHATTACHARYA – ACTING DIRECTOR OF THE CDC
item.description: Dear Dr. Bhattacharya, As a retired clinical psychologist, I have spent the past five years trying to understand the psychological factors that contribute to firmly held institutional and professional beliefs, and why such beliefs can be so resistant to change even when new information emerges. The stronger the belief system, the more difficult it is to challenge, particularly within large institutions where policies, reputations, and careers have developed around long-standing assumptions.

item.title: India’s Clinical Trial Boom Risks Outpacing Patient Protection
item.description: India is preparing a massive expansion of its clinical research infrastructure, targeting 1,000 new trial sites backed by ?10,000 crore in public investment. But a recent investigative report by IndiaSpend reveals a troubling disconnect: patient protections, informed consent, and regulatory oversight are not keeping pace with ambition . The result is a system at risk of scaling volume before trust, exposing vulnerable populations to ethical lapses. Consent on Paper, Not in Practice

item.title: FDA Approves Lilly’s Oral GLP-1 Foundayo™ (Orforglipron): A Potential Disruptor in Obesity Care?
item.description: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Foundayo (orforglipron), a once-daily oral GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly and Company, for adults with obesity or overweight with comorbidities. In Phase 3 ATTAIN trials, patients lost ~12.4% body weight (~27 pounds) at the highest dose over 72 weeks, compared to <1% with placebo. item.title: From Risk to Revival: Lilly’s Centessa Deal Reignites CNS Ambitions
item.description: Eli Lilly and Company has struck a decisive bet on the biology of wakefulness, agreeing to acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals for $6.3bn upfront, with a further $1.5bn in contingent payments. The target is not revenues but mechanism: a suite of orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonists designed to modulate the brain’s sleep–wake circuitry.
